glossary.definition: A neural network is a computing structure loosely inspired by neurons in the brain: layers of simple units that pass signals to each other, strengthening or weakening those connections as they learn from examples. Picture a huge grid of light switches, wired together in layers, where training slowly adjusts which switches influence which other switches until the whole grid reliably lights up the correct "answer" pattern for a given input. It's the basic architecture underneath almost all modern AI, from image recognition to language models.

items.title: OpenAI is stepping back from NDAs for data center projects
items.summary: Following this week's midterms where voters resoundingly voiced their opposition to data center expansion , OpenAI today announced new commitments to communities where it is working on data center projects, including that it won't use non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) with public officials. Many data center projects have come under scrutiny for relying on NDAs to hide discussions between developers and local officials. The ChatGPT maker won’t use NDAs with public officials as part of its new data center community commitments. Following this week’s midterms where voters resoundingly voiced their opposition to data center expansion , OpenAI today announced new commitments to communities where it is working on data center projects, including that it won’t use non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) with public officials.

items.title: Airbnb says it’s launching an AI travel agent in the first half of 2027
items.summary: Airbnb says its upcoming AI agent will help travelers plan trips, compare options, manage bookings, and get assistance throughout their stay. Airbnb has teased its plans to build its own AI travel agent before, but on Thursday the company announced that the new AI feature will launch in the first half of 2027. In the company’s Q3 shareholder letter on Thursday , Airbnb also provided more detail about how the agent will work, what it will actually do, and how it’s different from a typical AI chatbot. In prior interviews, CEO Brian Chesky sketched out the travel company’s approach to AI, describing a plan to build an AI agent that has a richer interface than a conventional chatbot.

items.title: Ads in Chatbots Have Arrived. Here’s What’s Working—and What’s Not
items.summary: As Anthropic maintains its vow to keep ads out of Claude, the rest of the AI chatbot industry is racing to win over advertisers without antagonizing users. Anthropic is holding firm on the pledge made in its Super Bowl commercial this year to keep Claude ad-free. The company’s recent IPO filing didn’t even mention the possibility of selling ads to make money from the AI chatbot. It’s easy to maintain the high ground with about $112 billion in investor cash.

items.title: OpenAIs GPT-6 Cyber can both break into systems and propose how to fix them
items.summary: With GPT-6 Cyber, OpenAI is introducing an AI model built to find security vulnerabilities in software, develop exploits, and suggest patches. According to OpenAI, it has already found 81 previously unknown vulnerabilities in Firefox and developed 948 working exploits in the Linux kernel, significantly more than its predecessor. OpenAI has introduced GPT-6 Cyber, an AI model trained specifically to hunt for security vulnerabilities in software. OpenAI says the model can find flaws, build working exploits, and suggest patches.

items.title: Meta says US users can now video chat with their Muse AI avatar
items.summary: Meta's AI agent can now take calls as a customizable animated avatar, ahead of the launch of a Tamagotchi-like wearable designed to bring Muse to life. , the company announced on Thursday. First introduced at Meta’s Connect developer conference in September, the video-chatting feature involves new AI models, Muse Realtime Avatar and Muse Realtime Voice technology, which help power the digital avatar that chats with the user. While other AI competitors offer voice chat features, Meta’s Muse offers a cute, animated avatar (nicknamed Jolly), which users interact with as they ask questions or request tasks to be handled on their behalf.

items.title: AWS launches Kiro bots to help devs coordinate AI coding agents
items.summary: AWS on Thursday launched Kiro bots, generally available within Kiro Crew, its open-source multi-agent development environment, to help developers coordinate parallel coding tasks, maintain context across sessions, and automate recurring software development workflows. Kiro bots are designed to take responsibility for specific parts of a developer’s workflow rather than execute isolated tasks within individual agent sessions, in turn addressing the growing coordination burden developers face as they increasingly rely on multiple AI agents to handle software development tasks in parallel, AWS said in a statement. Setting up bots and how do they work Developers can create a bot by opening the Customize section in Kiro Crew and selecting the “Add a bot” option, where they can choose either a default agent or an existing custom agent as its foundation. Each bot can be assigned a specific responsibility, such as issue triage, build monitoring, or release readiness, and customized with its own name, avatar, instructions, tools, and permissions based on the tasks it is expected to handle, the hyperscaler said.

items.title: Smartsheet’s new AI tool tracks corporate strategies, suggests fixes
items.summary: Work management software vendor Smartsheet has launched a new tool to help executives oversee company-wide strategies, with AI agents that monitor progress, identify problems, and recommend fixes. vsActual, announced Wednesday at Smartsheet’s Engage event, is a standalone “AI-native” application, separate from the company’s core work management software. It pulls data from a variety of business applications, including Oracle, Salesforce, SAP, and Workday, as well as work management tools such as Smartsheet itself. vsActual uses AI agents that carry out tasks on behalf of users, either in response to natural language prompts or running automatically in the background.

items.title: University of Utah retains operational sovereignty as Redtail expands research access
items.summary: Operational sovereignty gives universities authority over how shared computing resources are allocated, managed and secured. The University of Utah’s Redtail AI factory supercomputer brings advanced computing capabilities to a statewide community. Supporting researchers, students, administrators and external partners through that infrastructure requires more than computing capacity, according to Manish Parashar (pictured), chief AI officer of the University of Utah. “In research, we are always trying to balance research security with doing open research for societal good,” he said.

items.title: The Anthropic-Indian IT Partnership Is a Two-Way Bet
items.summary: Anthropic’s S-1 filing spends a long passage on competition. It names model developers such as OpenAI and Google, and first-party application providers. IT services firms do not appear. The passages on partners cite systems integrators (SIs) such as Accenture, Deloitte, KPMG and PwC. None is Indian.

items.title: Nintendo's biggest ROM chip supplier is bowing out of the business
items.summary: For years, the AI industry's insatiable demand for memory and storage has had plenty of knock-on effects on the price and availability of PC components like RAM , SSDs , and GPUs . Now those shortages are also squeezing the supply of ROM chips that power physical Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 game cartridges. Chip manufacturer Macronix announced in its third-quarter earnings report that the company's production of ROM chips "has reached its end" and that it will begin "gradually decoupling from the game industry," as reported by Taiwanese news site BigGo Finance . That could be an issue for Nintendo, which, analyst David Gibson notes, uses Macronix as its "main memory chip maker" for physical game cartridges.

items.title: Texas was the new epicenter of the AI data center buildout. That might be kaput.
items.summary: Texas is the fastest-growing data center market in the US and ground zero for Big Tech’s largest AI buildouts. But the blue wave that swept the Lone Star State may jeopardize that position. Democrat James Talarico won the US Senate seat against Ken Paxton. Gina Hinojosa won the race for governor against the Republican incumbent, Greg Abbott.
